pubs.note: Box Hill to Dorking on foot, the 2:34 to Victoria, then walked into Belgravia. First of the pair.
Two minutes on from the Grenadier. Out via Harrods food hall, home early.
Walked from Maltby St along Bermondsey Wall, past The Angel, into Rotherhithe on the south bank.
One stop from the Mayflower, under the Thames through Brunel's 1843 tunnel to the north bank. Windrush home to CJ.

board.text: Time Out's 50 best pubs vetted: The Lamb and Coach & Horses join the list; seven more go to Worth a detour. Seven Stars, French House and the Nag's Head were already on the list.
Worth a detour tier added: seven pubs with substance but no icon claim. Influencer gimmicks (Ship & Shovell, Aragon House, Cross Keys) cut.
Silver Cross Tavern (Westminster) and Newman Arms (Fitzrovia) added from the Georgian brothel crawl reel; the Cheshire Cheese gains its 1740s plaster-panel footnote. List is 24.
Blue Anchor (1722, by Hammersmith Bridge) pairs with The Dove: station, bridge, riverside walk, Dove.
Alternates: Holly Bush on the Heath day (can stand in for the Spaniards); Plume of Feathers (1691) on the Greenwich day, 5 min from the Trafalgar.
Churchill Arms pairing: the tick, then Sunday roast at the Fat Badger or pie at the Pelican, all in a 10-minute Notting Hill walk.
Old Bank of England (Fleet St, 1888 banking hall) is a pending candidate. It slots in by the Cheshire Cheese.
City cluster is a weekday play: Butler's Head, the Jampot, the Mitre and Cittie of Yorke all shut or limited at weekends.
Before any crawl, ask in the thread. Big football nights pack every pub in zones 1-2.

scouted.name: Old Bank of England
scouted.why: The 1888 Law Courts branch of the Bank of England, now a pub with a grand banking-hall interior. Your pending tier-one candidate.

scouted.name: The Holly Bush
scouted.why: Licensed 1807 in a 1790s house, a warren of dark rooms in Hampstead village. Heath-day alternate; can stand in for the Spaniards.

scouted.name: The Plume of Feathers
scouted.why: Greenwich's oldest pub, 1691, five minutes from the Trafalgar Tavern. Bonus stop on the riverboat day.

scouted.name: The Blue Anchor
scouted.why: Rowers' pub from 1722 at Hammersmith Bridge. Opens the Thames Path walk to the Dove.

scouted.name: The White Horse
scouted.why: Serious cask and bottle program with long-running beer festivals. The strongest beer destination off the list.

scouted.name: The Dog & Bell
scouted.why: Multiple-time CAMRA pub of the year for southeast London. A local's local with no tourist profile.

scouted.name: Williamson's Tavern
scouted.why: Former Lord Mayors' residence with gates gifted by William and Mary, by one claim the exact centre of the City. On the crawl line.

scouted.name: Shakespeares Head
scouted.why: Time Out's 2026 Pub of the Year. Opposite Sadler's Wells, with a big garden and performer photos on the walls. An easy evening from the King's Cross office.

scouted.name: The Cockpit
scouted.why: Handsome corner pub near St Paul's with history said to reach back to the 1500s. Three minutes from the Blackfriar.

scouted.name: Lord Clyde
scouted.why: Grade II listed, 1930s interior. Two minutes from the George Inn.

scouted.name: Windsor Castle
scouted.why: Victorian snob screens and tiny doors between the bars. About ten minutes from the Churchill Arms.

scouted.name: The Duke
scouted.why: Art deco mews pub with mahogany booths and old mirrors. A few minutes from The Lamb.

scouted.name: Southampton Arms
scouted.why: Victorian ale house on the edge of Hampstead Heath, known for dark wood and pork rolls. Fits the Heath day.

scouted.name: Carlton Tavern
scouted.why: Illegally demolished by a developer, then rebuilt brick by brick on council orders and reopened in 2021.
